# Rigging Module Framework: User Setup

The `user_setup` compound is where you define the topology of a module, meaning the control and joint hierarchies to be generated by this module, as well as the rest state of their transforms.

## How to create controls and joints

Controls and joints can be defined here using the dedicated `define_control` and `define_joint` nodes. These nodes can be daisy chained together to create transform chains. You can even create more complex hierarchies by branching them. The last node of each branch produced must be connected to the `control_definitions` or `joint_definitions` of the `set_definitions` node.

Note that controls and joints are always in separate hierarchies. It is not possible to parent a control under a joint or vice versa.

## How to parent something under a parent module's entity

When you want to parent something under a parent control or a parent joint from a connected parent module, you can use the `find_parent` node. This node allows you to search a parent entity either by tags or by name expression. The first matching parent entity will be returned as `parent_definition`, which can then be connected to the `parent_*` port of the `define_control` or `define_joint` nodes.

## How to use pins

Pins are helper transforms acting as guides that are set or passed on a module's inputs' `setup.pins`. You can use a pin's `pivot_matrix` and set it on the `pivot_matrix` of the `define_control` and `define_joint` nodes. You can manipulate them to produce new pivot matrices. For example, you could have two pins and interpolate a variable number of pivot matrices between them.

Pins can be accessed from the `setup_inputs`. You can access their data directly or you could use utility nodes such as `find_pin` and `find_all_pins`. These nodes allow you to find pins by searching them with name expression.

## How to use custom data

Custom data can be passed to the `user_setup` compound. The `custom` object on the `setup_inputs` is the same object that is passed on the module's inputs' `setup.custom`. You can use your custom data to do any kind of operations within the `user_setup`.

You can also create custom setup data which you can use in the `user_animation` compound. To do so, connect your object to the `custom` port of the `set_definitions` node. The custom setup is passed to the outputs so that it can also be used outside of this module. It can be accessed on the `outputs`' `setup.custom`.

# Rigging Module Framework: User Animation

The `user_animation` compound is where you update the transforms to do advanced transform operations, such as solving an IK.

At this point, the transform stacks are already computed, meaning that the transforms inherited the movement coming from parent modules and were also affected by their own operator matrices. Therefore, if a module does not require an animation solve, you could leave the `user_animation` untouched.

## How to access control and joint transforms

You can access a module's transforms using the dedicated `find_transform` and `find_all_transforms` nodes. These nodes allow you to search control or joint transforms either by tags or by name expression. Transform data can also be accessed directly from the `animation_inputs`.

## How to access attributes

You can access a module's attributes using the dedicated `find_attribute` and `find_all_attributes` nodes. These nodes allow you to search attributes of a matching type by name expression. Attribute data can also be accessed directly from the `animation_inputs`.

## How to use custom data

You can access both the custom setup and custom animation from the `animation_inputs.custom`. The `setup` object is the same object that was passed to the setup outputs in the `user_setup` compound, if any. The `animation` object is the same object that is passed to the module's inputs' `animation.custom`. You can use your animation custom data to do any kind of operations within the `user_animation` compound.

You can also create custom animation. To do so, connect your object to the `custom` port of the `set_update_settings` node. The custom animation is passed to the outputs so that it can also be used outside of this module. It can be accessed on the `outputs`' `animation.custom`.
